$comment: Handoff record for the next team or agent picking up this repository. Update the `updated` field and the relevant sections whenever the project changes materially. Read in this order: `status` for where things stand, `openItems` for what is owed (deploy-pages first — it is the one that can put an old resume in front of a client), `knownRisks` for the traps that have already cost someone a session, then `architecture` and `testing` before changing code. Every claim of verification here names how it was verified; if it does not say verified, treat it as unverified rather than assuming.
updatedBy: Claude (agent-assisted session), directed by Jay W. Snyder

project.name: SIGNAL
project.description: The interactive, gamified portfolio and resume of Jay W. Snyder. A hand-written Three.js rail shooter: six sectors down a neon corridor, each one a chapter of the resume sealed behind an encryption node. Fly the corridor, clear the resistance, break the node, read the dossier it was holding, continue. Ships with an equivalent written brief for accessibility, SEO, phones and visitors in a hurry.
project.audience: Business owners and operators evaluating whether to hire Jay to build AI systems for them. Secondary: recruiters and engineering leads.
project.goal: Convert. The site is the proof that Jay builds ambitious interactive software; the written brief is the escape hatch for anyone who just wants the facts.

owner.name: Jay W. Snyder
currentRoles: Director of Sales, Marketing & Technology, SkyRun Daytona Vacation Rentals

status: v3.1, merged to main on 2026-09-25: a juice-and-music pass. The drone soundtrack is replaced by an adaptive procedural score (src/core/Music.ts) — six tracks, one per sector, each in its own key and tempo, climbing 96 -> 124 BPM, with seven layers mixed live from the game's mood and the floor grid pulsing on the kick. Effects: hit-stop on kills and node breaks, a screen-space shockwave, warp-in arrivals, speed lines under boost, FOV punch, gun recoil, reticle hit markers, a kill chain and score popups. Engines now ease down in a fight, closing the hierarchy-inversion item. The finale's award total was hard-coded '/10' against fifteen awards and now reads the real count. READ openItems: the four stale branches are still there (this session's permission policy refused the delete), and the GitHub Pages mirror must be republished after every merge — it was, and verified, for this one.

config.note: vercel.json intentionally makes the build explicit rather than relying on Vercel's framework auto-detection, because this project's Vercel dashboard settings were configured for the previous React/CRA-era app and may not match. Dashboard settings are overridden by vercel.json.

githubPages.verificationMethod: 2026-09-25: `npm run deploy` from main; the gh-pages branch tree is byte-identical to dist/ (diff -r), and the live page served the new index bundle about 30 s after publishing.
githubPages.role: Mirror, not canonical. Serves identical bytes; index.html points canonical at the Vercel URL, which is exactly what canonical is for. Republish with `npm run deploy` whenever main changes, or retire it — nothing depends on it.
githubPages.note: Webfonts are self-hosted from public/fonts (see src/styles/fonts.css), so there are no third-party font requests to fail. An earlier version of this record warned about a blocked fonts.googleapis.com request; that was true of the pre-2026-09-03 build and is not true of any current one.

deployment.verificationMethod: Verified 2026-09-25 against the v3.1 merge (9a85515): `npm run build`, then SHA-256 of index.html and the four hashed JS/CSS assets fetched from the production origin all match dist/. Hashed assets carry `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, neither of which Vercel adds by default, so vercel.json is in effect. Redo it the same way after any merge.
deployment.browserVerification: The built bundle is driven in headless Chromium by `npm run smoke` on every change; 47 checks, all passing on the 2026-09-25 v3.1 merge. That runs against a locally served dist/, not against the production origin: the sandbox relay resets Chromium's TLS tunnel to external hosts, so a browser pass against the live URL has to be done from a normal network.

stack.rendering: Three.js r180, hand-written engine (no React, no react-three-fiber)
stack.styling: Plain CSS with custom-property design tokens (no Tailwind)

bundleSize.note: Run `npm run build` for current figures. Three is split into its own chunk via rollupOptions.manualChunks so app changes do not invalidate it, and SMAAPass is a lazy dynamic import because its lookup textures are ~38 kB gzipped and only the top quality tier uses it.

commands.note: `npm run build` runs `tsc --noEmit` first, so a type error fails the build. `npm run smoke` drives the built site in headless Chromium; serve dist first with `npm run smoke:serve`. Set SKIP_PASSIVE=1 to skip the slow passive-visitor check, and CHROMIUM_PATH if Playwright cannot find a browser. Playwright and http-server are now real devDependencies — `npm run smoke` used to fail on a fresh clone because neither was declared.

architecture.loop: Fixed-step simulation at 60 Hz with an accumulator and a 5-step cap, decoupled from rendering. Frame rate never changes flight feel, weapon cadence or collision. The whole route is 3654 m; at cruise that is about 56 seconds of flying end to end, or 39 with the faster transit a replay gets.

directories.src/core: Engine (renderer, post chain, adaptive quality tiers), Input, Audio (effects bus, limiter, level meter), Music (the adaptive score), Events bus, Save, Math helpers
directories.src/shaders: Fresnel hull material with in-shader fog and procedural panel lines; the composite post pass
directories.src/fx: Pooled GPU particles, shockwave/flash impacts, camera-facing ribbon trails, camera-space speed lines
directories.src/world: Route (the flight spline), Sector nodes, Landmarks, Corridor gates, Causeway floor, Environment props, Nebula, Starfield, Labels
directories.src/player: Rail flight model and the chase camera rig
directories.src/game: GameState (XP, ranks, shards, achievements), Combat, Pickups, Mission director
directories.src/ui: HUD, Codex dossier, Terminal, Toasts, Boot, TopBar, Brief, MissionCard, Overlay, TouchControls, Complete
directories.src/data: ALL CONTENT. Nothing user-visible is hard-coded elsewhere.
directories.scripts: smoke.mjs — behavioural regression checks, one per bug that actually shipped

notableTechniques: The route is an arc-length-parameterised spline. Forward motion is automatic and monotonic; steering only moves the ship inside a tube around the centreline, so a visitor cannot get lost or fly out of the content.

The mission director runs the same five beats six times — travel, waves, node, dossier, continue — so there is exactly one objective at any moment and the HUD always names it. Every entry into that script (launch, resume, Continue, a route-spine jump, a replay, a progress wipe) goes through one `beginSector` so they cannot drift apart, and every sector ends in a dossier: a node that is already open is handed back rather than flown past.

Stall assist: if a fight stops progressing the interface escalates, first an instruction, then automatic fire, then an explicit offer to open the dossier anyway. Nobody is locked out of a resume for being bad at a game.
The player cannot lose. Hits cost hull integrity, which regenerates.
Fresnel hull shader with FogExp2 implemented in-shader (custom ShaderMaterials do not get three fog for free) and triplanar procedural panel lines.
Causeway: a ribbon swept along the route spline, ruled with a grid, giving the corridor a floor and a vanishing point.
Adaptive quality governor steps pixel ratio, bloom, particle budget and prop density down a tier rather than stuttering. SMAA on the top tier is lazily imported.
Composite post pass driven by gameplay: boost streaks, damage vignette, explosion punch.

Adaptive procedural score (src/core/Music.ts). The game sets a mood each frame (silent, title, travel, combat, boss, dossier, paused, finale) from what is actually on screen; each mood is a gain per layer (pad, arp, bass, kick, snare, hat, lead) plus a bus cutoff. A 25 ms timer schedules the next 200 ms of sixteenths on the audio clock. Track changes land on the next downbeat, stingers on the next sixteenth. Harmony is chord-relative, so the lead and every in-key effect (shard chimes, kill-chain pitches, the detonation flourish) can never clash with the progression.
Sidechain pump: every kick automates one dedicated gain node that the pad, arp, bass and lead pass through. Only kicks touch it, so it never fights the mood fades for a parameter.
Audio-reactive floor: Music.pulse() reads the latest kick that has already sounded on the audio clock (not the scheduler, which runs 200 ms ahead) and the causeway's major rules brighten on it.

Hit-stop: main.ts scales the simulation, particles, impacts and pickups by a dilation factor that drops on kills (0.12 for 35 ms), shield breaches and node breaks (0.15 for 240 ms) and eases back in real time. The camera is not dilated, so shake and FOV punch land at full speed over a held frame.

Composite pass extras: an aspect-corrected refraction ring projected from a world position (Engine.shockwave) and a warp pulse on sector arrival (Engine.warp) that stretches the radial streak and tints the edges.
architecture.debugging: `window.SIGNAL.debug()` returns distance along the route, offset, speed, barrier, hull, mission phase, objective, hostiles, particle count, quality tier, per-node state, time dilation, kill chain, and the score's mood, track, BPM, bar and live output level in dBFS. `window.SIGNAL.goto(<sectorId>)` jumps to a sector; `window.SIGNAL.restart()` flies the corridor again from ORIGIN keeping progress; `window.SIGNAL.forceDossier()` opens the current dossier without fighting for it. `?tier=0|1|2` pins the quality tier.

bugsFixedDuringRebuild: The #ui overlay won on CSS specificity and swallowed all pointer events, which silently killed drag-to-fly on touch devices.
The written brief lived inside a fixed full-viewport overlay, so the page could not scroll and in-page anchors went nowhere.
Dossiers closed themselves a few seconds after arrival as the ship drifted out of the sector radius.
The ORIGIN torus knot rendered as an invisible dark silhouette: a smooth knot has no hard edges, so EdgesGeometry produced nothing to draw.
Arriving at a sector whose node was already open advanced the run on the spot, so a returning visitor — or anyone replaying — flew the whole corridor end to end and was shown none of the resume.

The completion card matched none of its own stylesheet: `.finale__*` in the markup against `.done__*` in the CSS. No width cap, no padding, no background, no scroll, and every call to action off screen.
The finale showed awards as 'N/10' from a hard-coded denominator while fifteen awards existed, so a thorough visitor's reward screen read '14/10'.

The boot screen's 'Compiling shaders' stage compiled almost nothing that matters in a fight: three's renderer.compile() walks visible objects only, and every pooled hostile, the node cores and the speed lines start hidden. The first wave compiled its materials on the spot, a hitch at the exact moment the first fight starts. warmUp now reveals hidden objects for the compile and restores them.

openItems.item: Republished and verified on 2026-09-25 for the v3.1 merge. It remains open as a standing rule, not a backlog item: GitHub Pages does not publish itself, so every merge to main needs `npm run deploy` or the mirror at knotenvy.github.io/Knotz3DPortfolio goes stale on an indexed URL. Retiring the mirror is the other clean option; leaving it stale is the bad one.

Still open as of 2026-09-25. Remote branches with zero commits not in main (verified with `git rev-list --count origin/main..<branch>` = 0 for each): claude/3d-portfolio-polish-8dxhjx, claude/gamified-3d-portfolio-r7vfyi, claude/portfolio-flight-sector-stops-jklu0u, update-node-version — plus this session's claude/laughing-wozniak-me03gw once its merge is in. Deleting them is lossless. Agent sessions have been refused twice now (HTTP 403 from the git proxy on an earlier session; the session permission policy on this one). Delete them from the GitHub branches page. Keep gh-pages: it is the Pages deploy target.

Partly addressed 2026-09-25. Boost now has discrete camera-space speed lines (src/fx/SpeedLines.ts) on top of the radial streak, which is what the 'fine speckle' note was asking for; confirm on real hardware that they read as speed rather than rain. The floor grid now pulses with the score, which restores some motion and chroma to fight frames, but the combat desaturation itself is unchanged. Per-sector prop silhouettes still share a material treatment and read as similar at distance.

Reviewers rate the look as a well-executed take on a familiar neon idiom rather than something visually novel. Round-3 remediation closed the concrete defects — the nebula renders, the sky has parallax, threat markers read over bloom, panel lines carry at distance — so what is left here is art direction rather than bugs: a distinctive material or lighting idea, or a less trodden palette.
GameState (XP, ranks, achievement conditions) has no unit coverage. A mis-awarded achievement shipped and was caught by review rather than by a test.

Reviewers noted the six sectors run the same script six times — fly, fight, break the node, read the dossier — which is deliberate and good for conversion, but nothing escalates mechanically across sectors 2-6 the way the visuals imply it might.

The finale bug was a class-name rename that stopped halfway between the stylesheet and the markup, and nothing in the toolchain can see that: TypeScript does not check class strings and CSS does not know what the DOM emits. A build-time diff of the class names the TS emits against the ones the CSS defines would have caught it in a second. Worth adding if another component is ever renamed.

The score was built and verified by measurement — mood transitions, a live output level on the final mix, a clean console — not by ear on real speakers. Listen through all six sectors once on headphones and on a laptop speaker. The levels most likely to want a nudge: MOODS in src/core/Music.ts (per-layer gains), the Music output gain (0.55), and the pad voice peak (0.034). Nothing else needs touching to rebalance the mix.

Music can be turned off independently of effects only from the terminal (`music off`); `M` and the toolbar button still mute everything. A visible music toggle in the pause panel would be friendlier for visitors who like the effects but not the score.

knownRisks: Both hosts must be republished together or they drift. Vercel redeploys automatically on push to main; GitHub Pages does not, and needs `npm run deploy`. If Pages is left stale it serves an old resume from an indexed URL.

Progress is stored in localStorage under the key `signal.save.v2`. Fields added since are filled in from defaults on load, so old saves still work; bumping the shape means bumping the version and the `v` check in src/core/Save.ts.
Custom ShaderMaterials do not receive three’s fog, lights or tone mapping automatically. Anything new that should sit in the same atmosphere has to implement fog itself, as src/shaders/hull.ts does.

Several bugs in this rebuild were of one shape: a factor in an alpha or intensity product silently going to zero, leaving an element rendering as nothing while looking correct in code. When something is invisible, check for a zeroed term before doubting the geometry.

#ui is a stack of fixed full-viewport layers over the canvas, and any one of them that takes pointer events becomes an invisible shield over everything beneath. base.css therefore lists which layers take pointers and defaults the rest to none. A new layer left off that list is visibly broken; a new layer wrongly added to it breaks everything under it silently. Three smoke checks assert the outcome.

Chromium interpolates a CSS transition or keyframe between a bare hex and a color-mix() through oklab(), and out-of-gamut midpoints can clip to a completely wrong hue — a violet objective card rendered a pure green ring for a whole animation. Both ends of any animated colour must be written with the same colour function.

Adding a uniform to a ShaderMaterial's uniforms object does not declare it in the GLSL. Miss the declaration and the shader fails to compile, the material draws nothing, and the game plays and reports identically — it looks like a tuning problem, not a broken shader. Check the console before tuning any effect that looks weak.

Emissive intensity is a deliberate hierarchy, not per-object taste: threats brightest (Enemy rim 2.4), then the ship (1.7), then the objective landmark (1.5), then scenery (0.62). Raising any one of them in isolation flattens the frame and the eye loses its focal point — reviewers reported exactly that when they were all near 1.0.

A dist/ mtime older than a commit does NOT mean the build is stale — the build runs before the commit. A reviewer inferred a stale-build process fault from exactly that and it was wrong. Verify what a bundle contains by grepping it or by measuring behaviour in the running app, never by comparing timestamps.

A CSS class rename is invisible to every check in this project. TypeScript does not type class strings, the CSS does not know what the DOM emits, and a behavioural test still passes because the elements are all present and clickable in the accessibility tree — the finale shipped unstyled for exactly this reason, on the one panel a visitor only reaches by finishing. When renaming a block, grep the other side.

`sector:decrypted` now carries `broken`. It is false when the ship simply flew back to a node that was already open, and anything that pays out — XP, the node count, the 'Unshaken' award, the detonation — must stay behind that flag or a visitor farms the same chapter by re-reading it.

Never time this product in a headless software renderer. Chromium on swiftshader runs the loop at a few frames a second and the fixed-step cap then advances sim time at a fraction of real time, which made a 56-second corridor look like four and a half minutes in a review of this very session. Time the forward model directly (it is self-contained arithmetic in Ship.step) or measure on real hardware.

The score's scheduler runs on a setInterval that browsers throttle to 1 Hz in a background tab, which would starve the 200 ms lookahead and play the music as a stutter. AudioEngine.setHidden suspends the context when the tab hides and resyncs the clock on return; keep that wired to visibilitychange.
Music.setMood is called every frame and is idempotent by design. Call it AFTER the simulation step: calling it before lagged a spawned wave by one frame, which the smoke suite caught.
Hit-stop dilates the simulation and effects but deliberately not the camera, the HUD, or the dossier timers. Anything new that should freeze on impact has to be fed simDt in main.ts, not dt.

A procedural audio bug is silent in every sense: a zeroed gain plays nothing and throws nothing. The level meter (AudioEngine.level, surfaced in SIGNAL.debug().music.level) is how you tell a quiet mix from a dead one; the smoke suite asserts it during a fight.

renderer.compile() uses traverseVisible. Anything added hidden (a pool, a lazily shown effect) is not pre-compiled unless it is inside the scene when warmUp runs — main.ts reveals hidden objects for that one call, so adding a new pooled effect to the scene before warmUp is enough.

The ship's engine bells, plume and intake now ease down with the same eased combat signal that dims the scenery (Ship.combat, fed from World.combat), rather than another static number. Full presence on the open road, stepped back behind hostiles when there are any.

Partial answer to the sector-escalation item: the score escalates across sectors (tempo 96 -> 124, busier hats in sectors 4-6, a lead line in every boss). The mechanics still run the same script six times.

testing.philosophy: Not coverage. Every check is a bug that actually shipped and that a type-checker, a linter and a screenshot all failed to notice. Add to it the same way: when something breaks in a browser, write the check that would have caught it. Two further rules earned the hard way: a check that can pass without observing the state it describes is worse than no check, because it reports green — assert that the test did its work, not just that nothing went wrong. And behavioural checks cannot see a material that failed to build, so the console is part of the suite.

testing.note: The passive-visitor check is timing-marginal on a software renderer. In a swiftshader sandbox it took 268s of its 300s budget on the pre-change build and 172s after, and it does fail there on a slow run — it is measuring how long an autofiring ship takes to kill a node at 2-5 fps, not the product. On real hardware it finishes in seconds. If it fails, re-run before believing it, and compare against the previous build rather than weakening the check. The audibility check reads the peak level over one second sampled in-page every 40 ms, not a single snapshot. In the swiftshader sandbox, single 43 ms snapshots taken through Playwright round-trips occasionally read near-silent (-77 to -98 dBFS) once per run, around the first wave, while a continuous 40 ms trace of the same fight never dropped below -56 dBFS and a fight with the mood frozen never did either. The cause was not pinned down; it did not reproduce with continuous sampling at either tier. If a listener ever reports the score dropping out at the first wave on real hardware, start there.
